sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation: Visa Eligibility
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: The live HTTPS page is published by the South Sudan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation on mofaic.gov.ss. Its WordPress API record says it was modified 5 December 2024 and supplies the Ministry’s country-by-country visa and fee table; it remains the destination authority’s current published schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Egypt EXEMPTED … Kenya EXEMPTED … Tanzania EXEMPTED … Uganda EXEMPTED.

sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation: Visas and requirements
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: The current MFA page on mofaic.gov.ss describes ordinary single-entry, transit and diplomatic/official/service routes, application requirements and stated exceptions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Others may be able to obtain entry visas upon arrival at any port of entry.

sources.title: South Sudan eVisa
sources.publisher: Ministry of Interior, Department of e-Visa and Immigration Service
sources.officialityEvidence: The live evisa.gov.ss portal, last modified 22 July 2026, identifies the Ministry of Interior, South Sudan National Police, Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration, and its Department of E-Visa and Immigration Service as the Government eServices operator.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Download your e-visa PDF from anywhere within 72 hours.

sources.title: South Sudan Trade Information Hub: Immigration services
sources.publisher: South Sudan Trade Information Hub, Ministry of Trade and Industry
sources.officialityEvidence: The live tradeinfohub.gov.ss page says the Hub is managed by the Ministry of Trade and Industry and publishes immigration service descriptions linked to the Ministry of Interior.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Most travelers can obtain visa on arrival; however, some nationalities may require a pre-approved visa.

sources.title: South Sudan Immigration eServices: visitor-account registration
sources.publisher: Ministry of Interior, Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration
sources.officialityEvidence: The live visitor-account form is on the Government eServices domain linked by the current official eVisa portal to its Immigration eVisa application service. It records a passport number and nationality, but it is an account-registration form and gives no visa-eligibility result or nationality route.

sources.title: EAC Common Market Protocol: free movement of persons
sources.officialityEvidence: The EAC Secretariat hosts this full Protocol text and its current visa-free-entry page identifies Article 7(1) as the basis for EAC Partner-State visa-free entry. Article 1 defines Partner States to include any country granted Community membership; Article 7(2)(a) says each Partner State shall ensure other Partner-State citizens enter without a visa.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Each Partner State shall ensure the entry of citizens of other Partner States … without a visa.

sources.title: East African Community: Visa-Free Entry
sources.officialityEvidence: The live EAC Secretariat immigration page says all Partner States are implementing Article 7(1) and describes visa-free entry for citizens travelling to other Partner States. It is regional primary guidance but does not give South Sudan’s individual operational exception or an ordinary-passport selector.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All Partner States are implementing Article 7(1) … visa-free entry of citizens of EAC Partner States.

sources.title: East African Community: Partner States
sources.officialityEvidence: The current EAC Secretariat page identifies the eight current Partner States, including Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Uganda and Tanzania. It supplies the membership scope needed to assess the Protocol and EAC guidance.
sources.supportingExcerpt: EAC Partner States: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Uganda and Tanzania.

sources.title: Passports and Immigration Act, 2011
sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs’ live laws register links this official Act PDF. Its entry rule requires a valid visa for an alien except as section 16 provides, while the Act and MFA guidance do not map a listed nationality to a single issuance channel.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Except as provided in section 16 below, no alien shall enter South Sudan unless he or she is in possession of a valid visa.

sources.title: Nationality Act, 2011
sources.publisher: Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs’ live laws register links this official Nationality Act PDF, which supplies the legal South Sudanese-national scope used for the citizenship classification.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The purpose of this Act is to provide a legal framework governing the acquisition and loss of South Sudanese Nationality.
